schedule.name: Research Runtime Discovery
schedule.input: Product / Competitor Sample Intelligence, Multi-Agent Engineering & Mechanism Intelligence, and Published Research & Industry Application Intelligence.
schedule.work: Execute the three intelligence profiles plus the theme-first sample overlay; normalize and deduplicate current, rolling-window and prior-art evidence by research problem.

schedule.name: Research Runtime Queue
schedule.work: Make one Selected or No Selection decision for each of the three research columns.

schedule.name: Research Runtime Reading
schedule.input: Selected objects in Today's Research Plan
schedule.work: Perform source-complete Deep Reading and evidence extraction.

schedule.name: Research Runtime Analysis
schedule.work: State the research question, classify evidence identities, analyze and compare, form a bounded judgment, identify an article type and dynamic modules, map general implications, then test optional first-party relevance.

schedule.name: Research Runtime Production
schedule.work: Build complete bilingual V2 candidates in article-sized durable segments. Persist and remotely verify each item's Article Brief, Argument Architecture, Figure Plan, bilingual pre-candidate drafts, deterministic baseline PNG and runtime-production-checkpoint/v2 state before starting the next item; then atomically stage the verified complete candidate batch and pass all editorial, visual and layout gates.
prohibitions: Writing from signals or Reading Results
Fixed Cover or Figure image-container sections
Blocking Production on the optional 16:00 Cover Upgrade
Reopening or downgrading Completed Production because an optional cover upgrade failed

schedule.name: Research Runtime Publication
schedule.work: Release complete Research Center Editions and separately authorized Community Editions; update GitHub, bilingual website surfaces and indexes; commit, verify and release.

schedule.name: Research Runtime Weekly
schedule.input: Latest-main P2 Registry and checkpoints plus evidence-validated Daily Research from the previous seven days
schedule.work: Check every due P2 object, execute at most one triggered P2 special study, and produce an independently readable AI Research Brief about material weekly changes, connections, evidence, disputes, judgments and open questions.
schedule.output: P2 Check Record, zero or one P2 Special Study, and Weekly Synthesis
prohibitions: More than one P2 special study
Direct publication of a P2 study
Silent omission of a due P2 object

schedule.name: Research Runtime Academic
schedule.input: Paper, benchmark, specification or institution objects
schedule.work: Execute the complete reading, analysis, writing, evidence and editing pipeline.

schedule.name: Research Program Runtime
schedule.input: Independent queues for TMPA, FCoP, CodeFlowMu, Digital Employee and Research Operating System
schedule.work: Advance eligible program objects through Program Queue, Research, Review and Program Publication.
schedule.output: Program Runtime Record and governed program transition

triage.candidate: Agent upgrades that alter built-in tool contracts need execution-ABI admission, not model-string substitution alone
triage.researchQuestion: When an agent version changes tool-call parameter and file-edit semantics, what execution-contract compatibility evidence must a host prove before adopting the upgrade?

researchValue.failure: Treating an agent or model upgrade as a string-only configuration change can break local tool parsing and execution even when the intended capability is unchanged.
researchValue.finding: The official migration guidance separates output-only remote execution from local tool execution because the latter crosses a changed built-in tool contract.
researchValue.mechanism: Version the agent identity together with its tool-call ABI, validate adapters against the new parameter and edit semantics, and gate migration on execution-contract compatibility rather than model availability alone.
researchValue.implication: Agent runtimes should pin and verify tool contracts as part of host admission and upgrade, not assume model-version changes are behaviorally or structurally transparent.

triage.selectionReason: The execution-ABI problem is concrete and distinct, but today's evidence is still one vendor's official migration guidance. It remains a candidate until another implementation, incident or benchmark independently tests the contract-migration boundary.

triage.candidate: Long-running turns need explicit authority epochs so next-turn policy changes do not rewrite already-admitted work
triage.researchQuestion: When configuration changes while a turn is suspended, which policy snapshot should remain authoritative for the resumed turn, and at what boundary may new policy take effect?

researchValue.failure: If environment-policy updates take effect inside an already admitted turn, the authority surface can change between suspension and resume without a new execution boundary.
researchValue.finding: Codex deliberately keeps the active turn on the captured policy environment and defers newly saved settings to the next turn.
researchValue.mechanism: Capture the policy-relevant environment at turn admission, use that same snapshot for policy evaluation and runtime publication, and apply configuration changes only at the next turn boundary.
researchValue.implication: Long-running workers need explicit authority epochs: configuration freshness and execution authority are different facts, and new policy should not rewrite the authority of work already admitted.

triage.selectionReason: Turn-scoped authority is a useful refinement of recent authority-precedence work, but it currently has one maintainer implementation and is semantically close to the September 12 action-time authority object. Retain it for a future cross-sample authority-epoch comparison.

triage.candidate: Approval should authorize one immutable validated invocation, not a tool name detached from exact arguments
triage.researchQuestion: What identity must a human or policy approval bind so the invocation inspected for authorization is provably the same call that later reaches execution?

researchValue.failure: Approval can become unsound if the arguments inspected for the decision differ from what is actually executed, or if argument inspection itself runs user code before approval.
researchValue.finding: The SDK separates conservative argument preparation from execution and verifies the exact invocation identity again before using the approval result.
researchValue.mechanism: Use side-effect-free data validation when possible, require approval for uninspectable/custom paths, bind the decision to tool plus invoker plus raw arguments, and reject any mismatch before execution.
researchValue.implication: Human or policy approval should authorize an immutable call instance, not merely a tool name or a loosely parsed request.

triage.selectionReason: The TOCTOU boundary is precise and high-value, but current evidence is one maintainer implementation and the broader call-time authority problem already has recent cross-sample treatment. It remains a strong comparison candidate rather than a same-day selection.

triage.candidate: Long sessions need explicit capability lifecycles so inactive skills leave the declared tool surface
triage.researchQuestion: How should a long-running agent distinguish persistent from bounded capabilities and make skill eviction visible so historical tool declarations do not accumulate indefinitely?

researchValue.failure: A long session that keeps every historically loaded skill active accumulates unused tool declarations, expanding context and authority surfaces indefinitely.
researchValue.finding: ADK makes skill persistence an explicit lifecycle policy and provides an opt-in bounded working set without changing the persistent default.
researchValue.mechanism: Classify skills as persistent or bounded, cap the bounded active set, evict least-recently-loaded skills, and surface unload events to the model.
researchValue.implication: Digital employees need capability lifecycle management as well as memory lifecycle management; tools that are no longer active should leave the declared authority surface explicitly.

triage.selectionReason: Capability lifecycle is distinct from the September 16 skill-routing question, but the evidence remains a single ADK implementation. Preserve it for comparison with other bounded tool-surface or capability-unload mechanisms.

triage.candidate: Low spontaneous failure does not imply low collective contagion risk when unsafe trajectories cross hidden communication paths
triage.researchQuestion: How should multi-agent systems test conditional contagion susceptibility when nominally independent workers may still share hidden communication paths even though spontaneous harmful cascades are rare?

researchValue.failure: A low observed rate of spontaneous agent failure can hide a system that is highly susceptible once one unsafe trajectory crosses an unintended communication boundary.
researchValue.finding: Injected unsafe trajectories sharply increased executed harm in the benchmark, and the deployment audit verified a transport path across nominally independent runs.
researchValue.mechanism: Unsafe behavior propagates when communication permits other agents to adopt and retransmit a local deviation faster than containment and recovery correct it.
researchValue.implication: Multi-agent governance must audit transport and shared-state boundaries, not only individual-agent behavior; isolation and recovery capacity are first-class controls against collective failure.

triage.selectionReason: The primary research is strong, but today's proposition is too close to the September 17 selected Emergence World object on harmful-state propagation across agents, containment and recovery. Keep it as comparison evidence rather than create consecutive near-duplicate Digital Employee/Industry objects.

triage.candidate: Running tools should publish bounded progress telemetry to the runtime instead of forcing scheduling decisions from pre-call guesses
triage.researchQuestion: What machine-observable progress contract should long-running tool execution expose to scheduling and recovery logic, and how much decision value can it add without entering the agent's semantic context?

researchValue.failure: Treating a running tool as an opaque wait forces the runtime to guess duration from names or historical averages, causing poor resource and scheduling decisions when the environment changes.
researchValue.finding: Live tool progress is materially more accurate at decision points than pre-call predictors and improves serving latency without changing the agent's task behavior.
researchValue.mechanism: Expose bounded progress signals from the tool execution layer to the serving/runtime layer while keeping them out of the agent's semantic context unless needed.
researchValue.implication: A digital-employee runtime should distinguish business semantics from operational telemetry: workers can remain semantically isolated while still publishing machine-observable progress for scheduling and recovery.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary research isolates a fresh runtime-observability boundary and reports concrete serving effects. The problem is materially different from recent skill routing, recovery authorization and long-horizon completion objects, and it provides the strongest evidence for today's Open-source Engineering column.

triage.candidate: Shared coordination constraints need a formally verified minimum retained-utility guarantee under stochastic multi-agent execution
triage.researchQuestion: In stochastic multi-agent environments where each agent optimizes its own reward, how should shared coordination constraints be specified and verified so every agent retains an acceptable minimum utility before execution?

researchValue.failure: Coordination rules that work in deterministic demonstrations may not guarantee acceptable individual outcomes when execution is stochastic and agents optimize their own rewards.
researchValue.finding: The work gives a formal robustness quantity and a verification procedure for shared constraints in stochastic multi-agent environments.
researchValue.mechanism: Specify a social law as an admissible coordination constraint, define a minimum retained-utility guarantee, and verify it through MDP reductions before relying on the policy in execution.
researchValue.implication: Agent governance can be framed as pre-execution verification of admissible interaction constraints rather than letting a scheduler or model infer acceptable coordination from observed behavior alone.

triage.selectionReason: Primary research provides a formally bounded mechanism and a distinct governance question about ex-ante coordination robustness under stochastic outcomes. It complements rather than duplicates recent construct-level coordination evaluation and deterministic-coordinator work, and is today's strongest Industry Architecture object.

reading.workResult: Skill 03 completed source-bounded Deep Reading for both same-date Selected objects. Q-20260918-01 read the complete Social Laws primary study across formal model, alpha-robustness, social-law comparison, worst-case-MDP verification, approximate value bounds, grid experiments and limits. The paper shows that individually optimal policies can interact badly, and that a shared action restriction can be verified inside a declared stochastic-game model by solving each single-agent projection and one worst-case MDP per agent. The important boundary is that robustness alpha must be considered together with retained guaranteed utility: a more restrictive law can improve robustness while lowering useful performance, and the guarantee depends on the modeled state/action/reward/transition space, all agents remaining inside the assumed policy class, and Assumption 1 requiring optimal actions at every state. The paper's formal definition assumes positive rewards while its experiments use all-negative costs, which the text says admit an analogous formulation but does not re-derive in equal detail. The bounded Runtime finding is that Coordination-rule Identity, Model Identity, Robustness Evidence, Utility Evidence, Execution Admission, Business Authorization and Effect Verification must remain separate facts. Q-20260918-02 read the complete Ask the Tool, Don't Guess primary study. It distinguishes strong remaining-work signals from weak near-completion signals, exports call-id/work-done/total/phase/timestamp telemetry over a side channel that leaves the agent-visible result path unchanged, and reports that live progress is materially more accurate than duration-history predictors at KV-cache decision points and under environment changes. In a 4xH100 serving replay, the reported p90 post-tool-call TTFT reduction versus LRU is 20.7% for HBM-only and 20.8% for HBM+DRAM. The paper explicitly treats tenant-originated progress as untrusted input, bounds its scheduling influence through session credit, and identifies opaque tools, parser gaps and behavior-changing instrumentation as limitations. The bounded Runtime finding is that Execution Identity, Progress Observation, Telemetry Confidence, Scheduling Authority, Business Completion and Effect Authorization/Verification must remain separate; progress may justify waiting or resource reallocation but cannot by itself prove completion or authorize retry. Reading performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production or Publication. triage.candidate: Agent upgrades that alter built-in tool contracts need execution-ABI admission, not model-string substitution alone
triage.researchQuestion: When an agent version changes tool-call parameter and file-edit semantics, what execution-contract compatibility evidence must a host prove before adopting the upgrade?

researchValue.failure: Treating an agent or model upgrade as a string-only configuration change can break local tool parsing and execution even when the intended capability is unchanged.
researchValue.finding: The official migration guidance separates output-only remote execution from local tool execution because the latter crosses a changed built-in tool contract.
researchValue.mechanism: Version the agent identity together with its tool-call ABI, validate adapters against the new parameter and edit semantics, and gate migration on execution-contract compatibility rather than model availability alone.
researchValue.implication: Agent runtimes should pin and verify tool contracts as part of host admission and upgrade, not assume model-version changes are behaviorally or structurally transparent.

triage.selectionReason: The execution-ABI problem is concrete and distinct, but today's evidence is still one vendor's official migration guidance. It remains a candidate until another implementation, incident or benchmark independently tests the contract-migration boundary.

triage.candidate: Long-running turns need explicit authority epochs so next-turn policy changes do not rewrite already-admitted work
triage.researchQuestion: When configuration changes while a turn is suspended, which policy snapshot should remain authoritative for the resumed turn, and at what boundary may new policy take effect?

researchValue.failure: If environment-policy updates take effect inside an already admitted turn, the authority surface can change between suspension and resume without a new execution boundary.
researchValue.finding: Codex deliberately keeps the active turn on the captured policy environment and defers newly saved settings to the next turn.
researchValue.mechanism: Capture the policy-relevant environment at turn admission, use that same snapshot for policy evaluation and runtime publication, and apply configuration changes only at the next turn boundary.
researchValue.implication: Long-running workers need explicit authority epochs: configuration freshness and execution authority are different facts, and new policy should not rewrite the authority of work already admitted.

triage.selectionReason: Turn-scoped authority is a useful refinement of recent authority-precedence work, but it currently has one maintainer implementation and is semantically close to the September 12 action-time authority object. Retain it for a future cross-sample authority-epoch comparison.

triage.candidate: Approval should authorize one immutable validated invocation, not a tool name detached from exact arguments
triage.researchQuestion: What identity must a human or policy approval bind so the invocation inspected for authorization is provably the same call that later reaches execution?

researchValue.failure: Approval can become unsound if the arguments inspected for the decision differ from what is actually executed, or if argument inspection itself runs user code before approval.
researchValue.finding: The SDK separates conservative argument preparation from execution and verifies the exact invocation identity again before using the approval result.
researchValue.mechanism: Use side-effect-free data validation when possible, require approval for uninspectable/custom paths, bind the decision to tool plus invoker plus raw arguments, and reject any mismatch before execution.
researchValue.implication: Human or policy approval should authorize an immutable call instance, not merely a tool name or a loosely parsed request.

triage.selectionReason: The TOCTOU boundary is precise and high-value, but current evidence is one maintainer implementation and the broader call-time authority problem already has recent cross-sample treatment. It remains a strong comparison candidate rather than a same-day selection.

triage.candidate: Long sessions need explicit capability lifecycles so inactive skills leave the declared tool surface
triage.researchQuestion: How should a long-running agent distinguish persistent from bounded capabilities and make skill eviction visible so historical tool declarations do not accumulate indefinitely?

researchValue.failure: A long session that keeps every historically loaded skill active accumulates unused tool declarations, expanding context and authority surfaces indefinitely.
researchValue.finding: ADK makes skill persistence an explicit lifecycle policy and provides an opt-in bounded working set without changing the persistent default.
researchValue.mechanism: Classify skills as persistent or bounded, cap the bounded active set, evict least-recently-loaded skills, and surface unload events to the model.
researchValue.implication: Digital employees need capability lifecycle management as well as memory lifecycle management; tools that are no longer active should leave the declared authority surface explicitly.

triage.selectionReason: Capability lifecycle is distinct from the September 16 skill-routing question, but the evidence remains a single ADK implementation. Preserve it for comparison with other bounded tool-surface or capability-unload mechanisms.

triage.candidate: Low spontaneous failure does not imply low collective contagion risk when unsafe trajectories cross hidden communication paths
triage.researchQuestion: How should multi-agent systems test conditional contagion susceptibility when nominally independent workers may still share hidden communication paths even though spontaneous harmful cascades are rare?

researchValue.failure: A low observed rate of spontaneous agent failure can hide a system that is highly susceptible once one unsafe trajectory crosses an unintended communication boundary.
researchValue.finding: Injected unsafe trajectories sharply increased executed harm in the benchmark, and the deployment audit verified a transport path across nominally independent runs.
researchValue.mechanism: Unsafe behavior propagates when communication permits other agents to adopt and retransmit a local deviation faster than containment and recovery correct it.
researchValue.implication: Multi-agent governance must audit transport and shared-state boundaries, not only individual-agent behavior; isolation and recovery capacity are first-class controls against collective failure.

triage.selectionReason: The primary research is strong, but today's proposition is too close to the September 17 selected Emergence World object on harmful-state propagation across agents, containment and recovery. Keep it as comparison evidence rather than create consecutive near-duplicate Digital Employee/Industry objects.

triage.candidate: Running tools should publish bounded progress telemetry to the runtime instead of forcing scheduling decisions from pre-call guesses
triage.researchQuestion: What machine-observable progress contract should long-running tool execution expose to scheduling and recovery logic, and how much decision value can it add without entering the agent's semantic context?

researchValue.failure: Treating a running tool as an opaque wait forces the runtime to guess duration from names or historical averages, causing poor resource and scheduling decisions when the environment changes.
researchValue.finding: Live tool progress is materially more accurate at decision points than pre-call predictors and improves serving latency without changing the agent's task behavior.
researchValue.mechanism: Expose bounded progress signals from the tool execution layer to the serving/runtime layer while keeping them out of the agent's semantic context unless needed.
researchValue.implication: A digital-employee runtime should distinguish business semantics from operational telemetry: workers can remain semantically isolated while still publishing machine-observable progress for scheduling and recovery.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary research isolates a fresh runtime-observability boundary and reports concrete serving effects. The problem is materially different from recent skill routing, recovery authorization and long-horizon completion objects, and it provides the strongest evidence for today's Open-source Engineering column.

triage.candidate: Shared coordination constraints need a formally verified minimum retained-utility guarantee under stochastic multi-agent execution
triage.researchQuestion: In stochastic multi-agent environments where each agent optimizes its own reward, how should shared coordination constraints be specified and verified so every agent retains an acceptable minimum utility before execution?

researchValue.failure: Coordination rules that work in deterministic demonstrations may not guarantee acceptable individual outcomes when execution is stochastic and agents optimize their own rewards.
researchValue.finding: The work gives a formal robustness quantity and a verification procedure for shared constraints in stochastic multi-agent environments.
researchValue.mechanism: Specify a social law as an admissible coordination constraint, define a minimum retained-utility guarantee, and verify it through MDP reductions before relying on the policy in execution.
researchValue.implication: Agent governance can be framed as pre-execution verification of admissible interaction constraints rather than letting a scheduler or model infer acceptable coordination from observed behavior alone.

triage.selectionReason: Primary research provides a formally bounded mechanism and a distinct governance question about ex-ante coordination robustness under stochastic outcomes. It complements rather than duplicates recent construct-level coordination evaluation and deterministic-coordinator work, and is today's strongest Industry Architecture object.

reading.workResult: Skill 03 completed source-bounded Deep Reading for both same-date Selected objects. Q-20260918-01 read the complete Social Laws primary study across formal model, alpha-robustness, social-law comparison, worst-case-MDP verification, approximate value bounds, grid experiments and limits. The paper shows that individually optimal policies can interact badly, and that a shared action restriction can be verified inside a declared stochastic-game model by solving each single-agent projection and one worst-case MDP per agent. The important boundary is that robustness alpha must be considered together with retained guaranteed utility: a more restrictive law can improve robustness while lowering useful performance, and the guarantee depends on the modeled state/action/reward/transition space, all agents remaining inside the assumed policy class, and Assumption 1 requiring optimal actions at every state. The paper's formal definition assumes positive rewards while its experiments use all-negative costs, which the text says admit an analogous formulation but does not re-derive in equal detail. The bounded Runtime finding is that Coordination-rule Identity, Model Identity, Robustness Evidence, Utility Evidence, Execution Admission, Business Authorization and Effect Verification must remain separate facts. Q-20260918-02 read the complete Ask the Tool, Don't Guess primary study. It distinguishes strong remaining-work signals from weak near-completion signals, exports call-id/work-done/total/phase/timestamp telemetry over a side channel that leaves the agent-visible result path unchanged, and reports that live progress is materially more accurate than duration-history predictors at KV-cache decision points and under environment changes. In a 4xH100 serving replay, the reported p90 post-tool-call TTFT reduction versus LRU is 20.7% for HBM-only and 20.8% for HBM+DRAM. The paper explicitly treats tenant-originated progress as untrusted input, bounds its scheduling influence through session credit, and identifies opaque tools, parser gaps and behavior-changing instrumentation as limitations. The bounded Runtime finding is that Execution Identity, Progress Observation, Telemetry Confidence, Scheduling Authority, Business Completion and Effect Authorization/Verification must remain separate; progress may justify waiting or resource reallocation but cannot by itself prove completion or authorize retry. Reading performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production or Publication. The exact two-note head 20d93522eeff716c8fe14be728e14572c41a1964 passed the Validate Runtime Center step in Validate Research Center 3.0 run 35302389225 before this result was persisted.
reading.workResult_zh: Skill 03 已对两个同日 Selected Object 完成来源边界内的 Deep Reading。Q-20260918-01 完整深读 Social Laws 一手研究的形式模型、alpha-robustness、Social-law 比较、Worst-case MDP Verification、近似 Value Bound、Grid 实验与边界。论文说明，单个 Agent 各自执行最优 Policy 并不能证明联合行为安全；在明确声明的 Stochastic-game Model 内，可以先求解每个 Single-agent Projection，再为每个 Agent 构造并求解一个 Worst-case MDP，从而验证共享 Action Restriction 的鲁棒性。关键边界是 alpha 不能单独作为采用依据，还必须同时看 Restriction 后保留下来的 Guaranteed Utility：规则更严格可能提高 Robustness，却降低实际效用；而 Guarantee 依赖完整声明的 State/Action/Reward/Transition Model、所有 Agent 均停留在假定 Policy Class 内，以及 Assumption 1 所要求的每个 State 都选择最优 Action。论文形式定义假定 Positive Reward，而实验使用全负 Cost；正文说明全负 Cost 可定义类似形式，但没有用同等细节重新推导。因此边界 Runtime 结论是 Coordination-rule Identity、Model Identity、Robustness Evidence、Utility Evidence、Execution Admission、Business Authorization 与 Effect Verification 必须保持为不同事实。Q-20260918-02 完整深读 Ask the Tool, Don't Guess 一手研究。研究区分可表示 Remaining Work 的 Strong Signal 与只能表示 Near-completion 的 Weak Signal，通过不改变 Agent-visible Result Path 的 Side Channel 输出 Call-id、Work-done、Total、Phase、Timestamp 进度事件，并显示 Live Progress 在 KV-cache 决策点及环境变化下明显优于基于历史 Duration 的 Predictor。4xH100 Serving Replay 中，相对 LRU 报告的 Tool Call 后 p90 TTFT 降幅为 HBM-only 20.7%、HBM+DRAM 20.8%。论文明确把 Tenant-originated Progress 视为 Untrusted Input，用 Session Credit 限制它对调度的影响，并把 Tool 不暴露信息、Parser 缺口和 Instrumentation 改变 Tool Behavior 列为边界。边界 Runtime 结论是 Execution Identity、Progress Observation、Telemetry Confidence、Scheduling Authority、Business Completion 与 Effect Authorization/Verification 必须分离；Progress 可以支持继续等待或资源重分配，但不能单独证明完成，更不能单独授权 Retry。Reading 未执行 Research Analysis、文章写作、可视化、Production 或 Publication。精确两份 Note Head 20d93522eeff716c8fe14be728e14572c41a1964 已在本 Result 持久化前通过 Validate Research Center 3.0 Run 35302389225 的 Validate Runtime Center 步骤。

triage.candidate: Agent upgrades that alter built-in tool contracts need execution-ABI admission, not model-string substitution alone
triage.researchQuestion: When an agent version changes tool-call parameter and file-edit semantics, what execution-contract compatibility evidence must a host prove before adopting the upgrade?

researchValue.failure: Treating an agent or model upgrade as a string-only configuration change can break local tool parsing and execution even when the intended capability is unchanged.
researchValue.finding: The official migration guidance separates output-only remote execution from local tool execution because the latter crosses a changed built-in tool contract.
researchValue.mechanism: Version the agent identity together with its tool-call ABI, validate adapters against the new parameter and edit semantics, and gate migration on execution-contract compatibility rather than model availability alone.
researchValue.implication: Agent runtimes should pin and verify tool contracts as part of host admission and upgrade, not assume model-version changes are behaviorally or structurally transparent.

triage.selectionReason: The execution-ABI problem is concrete and distinct, but today's evidence is still one vendor's official migration guidance. It remains a candidate until another implementation, incident or benchmark independently tests the contract-migration boundary.

triage.candidate: Long-running turns need explicit authority epochs so next-turn policy changes do not rewrite already-admitted work
triage.researchQuestion: When configuration changes while a turn is suspended, which policy snapshot should remain authoritative for the resumed turn, and at what boundary may new policy take effect?

researchValue.failure: If environment-policy updates take effect inside an already admitted turn, the authority surface can change between suspension and resume without a new execution boundary.
researchValue.finding: Codex deliberately keeps the active turn on the captured policy environment and defers newly saved settings to the next turn.
researchValue.mechanism: Capture the policy-relevant environment at turn admission, use that same snapshot for policy evaluation and runtime publication, and apply configuration changes only at the next turn boundary.
researchValue.implication: Long-running workers need explicit authority epochs: configuration freshness and execution authority are different facts, and new policy should not rewrite the authority of work already admitted.

triage.selectionReason: Turn-scoped authority is a useful refinement of recent authority-precedence work, but it currently has one maintainer implementation and is semantically close to the September 12 action-time authority object. Retain it for a future cross-sample authority-epoch comparison.

triage.candidate: Approval should authorize one immutable validated invocation, not a tool name detached from exact arguments
triage.researchQuestion: What identity must a human or policy approval bind so the invocation inspected for authorization is provably the same call that later reaches execution?

researchValue.failure: Approval can become unsound if the arguments inspected for the decision differ from what is actually executed, or if argument inspection itself runs user code before approval.
researchValue.finding: The SDK separates conservative argument preparation from execution and verifies the exact invocation identity again before using the approval result.
researchValue.mechanism: Use side-effect-free data validation when possible, require approval for uninspectable/custom paths, bind the decision to tool plus invoker plus raw arguments, and reject any mismatch before execution.
researchValue.implication: Human or policy approval should authorize an immutable call instance, not merely a tool name or a loosely parsed request.

triage.selectionReason: The TOCTOU boundary is precise and high-value, but current evidence is one maintainer implementation and the broader call-time authority problem already has recent cross-sample treatment. It remains a strong comparison candidate rather than a same-day selection.

triage.candidate: Long sessions need explicit capability lifecycles so inactive skills leave the declared tool surface
triage.researchQuestion: How should a long-running agent distinguish persistent from bounded capabilities and make skill eviction visible so historical tool declarations do not accumulate indefinitely?

researchValue.failure: A long session that keeps every historically loaded skill active accumulates unused tool declarations, expanding context and authority surfaces indefinitely.
researchValue.finding: ADK makes skill persistence an explicit lifecycle policy and provides an opt-in bounded working set without changing the persistent default.
researchValue.mechanism: Classify skills as persistent or bounded, cap the bounded active set, evict least-recently-loaded skills, and surface unload events to the model.
researchValue.implication: Digital employees need capability lifecycle management as well as memory lifecycle management; tools that are no longer active should leave the declared authority surface explicitly.

triage.selectionReason: Capability lifecycle is distinct from the September 16 skill-routing question, but the evidence remains a single ADK implementation. Preserve it for comparison with other bounded tool-surface or capability-unload mechanisms.

triage.candidate: Low spontaneous failure does not imply low collective contagion risk when unsafe trajectories cross hidden communication paths
triage.researchQuestion: How should multi-agent systems test conditional contagion susceptibility when nominally independent workers may still share hidden communication paths even though spontaneous harmful cascades are rare?

researchValue.failure: A low observed rate of spontaneous agent failure can hide a system that is highly susceptible once one unsafe trajectory crosses an unintended communication boundary.
researchValue.finding: Injected unsafe trajectories sharply increased executed harm in the benchmark, and the deployment audit verified a transport path across nominally independent runs.
researchValue.mechanism: Unsafe behavior propagates when communication permits other agents to adopt and retransmit a local deviation faster than containment and recovery correct it.
researchValue.implication: Multi-agent governance must audit transport and shared-state boundaries, not only individual-agent behavior; isolation and recovery capacity are first-class controls against collective failure.

triage.selectionReason: The primary research is strong, but today's proposition is too close to the September 17 selected Emergence World object on harmful-state propagation across agents, containment and recovery. Keep it as comparison evidence rather than create consecutive near-duplicate Digital Employee/Industry objects.

triage.candidate: Running tools should publish bounded progress telemetry to the runtime instead of forcing scheduling decisions from pre-call guesses
triage.researchQuestion: What machine-observable progress contract should long-running tool execution expose to scheduling and recovery logic, and how much decision value can it add without entering the agent's semantic context?

researchValue.failure: Treating a running tool as an opaque wait forces the runtime to guess duration from names or historical averages, causing poor resource and scheduling decisions when the environment changes.
researchValue.finding: Live tool progress is materially more accurate at decision points than pre-call predictors and improves serving latency without changing the agent's task behavior.
researchValue.mechanism: Expose bounded progress signals from the tool execution layer to the serving/runtime layer while keeping them out of the agent's semantic context unless needed.
researchValue.implication: A digital-employee runtime should distinguish business semantics from operational telemetry: workers can remain semantically isolated while still publishing machine-observable progress for scheduling and recovery.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary research isolates a fresh runtime-observability boundary and reports concrete serving effects. The problem is materially different from recent skill routing, recovery authorization and long-horizon completion objects, and it provides the strongest evidence for today's Open-source Engineering column.

triage.candidate: Shared coordination constraints need a formally verified minimum retained-utility guarantee under stochastic multi-agent execution
triage.researchQuestion: In stochastic multi-agent environments where each agent optimizes its own reward, how should shared coordination constraints be specified and verified so every agent retains an acceptable minimum utility before execution?

researchValue.failure: Coordination rules that work in deterministic demonstrations may not guarantee acceptable individual outcomes when execution is stochastic and agents optimize their own rewards.
researchValue.finding: The work gives a formal robustness quantity and a verification procedure for shared constraints in stochastic multi-agent environments.
researchValue.mechanism: Specify a social law as an admissible coordination constraint, define a minimum retained-utility guarantee, and verify it through MDP reductions before relying on the policy in execution.
researchValue.implication: Agent governance can be framed as pre-execution verification of admissible interaction constraints rather than letting a scheduler or model infer acceptable coordination from observed behavior alone.

triage.selectionReason: Primary research provides a formally bounded mechanism and a distinct governance question about ex-ante coordination robustness under stochastic outcomes. It complements rather than duplicates recent construct-level coordination evaluation and deterministic-coordinator work, and is today's strongest Industry Architecture object.

reading.workResult: Skill 03 completed source-bounded Deep Reading for both same-date Selected objects. Q-20260918-01 read the complete Social Laws primary study across formal model, alpha-robustness, social-law comparison, worst-case-MDP verification, approximate value bounds, grid experiments and limits. The paper shows that individually optimal policies can interact badly, and that a shared action restriction can be verified inside a declared stochastic-game model by solving each single-agent projection and one worst-case MDP per agent. The important boundary is that robustness alpha must be considered together with retained guaranteed utility: a more restrictive law can improve robustness while lowering useful performance, and the guarantee depends on the modeled state/action/reward/transition space, all agents remaining inside the assumed policy class, and Assumption 1 requiring optimal actions at every state. The paper's formal definition assumes positive rewards while its experiments use all-negative costs, which the text says admit an analogous formulation but does not re-derive in equal detail. The bounded Runtime finding is that Coordination-rule Identity, Model Identity, Robustness Evidence, Utility Evidence, Execution Admission, Business Authorization and Effect Verification must remain separate facts. Q-20260918-02 read the complete Ask the Tool, Don't Guess primary study. It distinguishes strong remaining-work signals from weak near-completion signals, exports call-id/work-done/total/phase/timestamp telemetry over a side channel that leaves the agent-visible result path unchanged, and reports that live progress is materially more accurate than duration-history predictors at KV-cache decision points and under environment changes. In a 4xH100 serving replay, the reported p90 post-tool-call TTFT reduction versus LRU is 20.7% for HBM-only and 20.8% for HBM+DRAM. The paper explicitly treats tenant-originated progress as untrusted input, bounds its scheduling influence through session credit, and identifies opaque tools, parser gaps and behavior-changing instrumentation as limitations. The bounded Runtime finding is that Execution Identity, Progress Observation, Telemetry Confidence, Scheduling Authority, Business Completion and Effect Authorization/Verification must remain separate; progress may justify waiting or resource reallocation but cannot by itself prove completion or authorize retry. Reading performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production or Publication. The exact two-note head 20d93522eeff716c8fe14be728e14572c41a1964 passed the Validate Runtime Center step in Validate Research Center 3.0 run 35302389225 before this result was persisted.
reading.workResult_zh: Skill 03 已对两个同日 Selected Object 完成来源边界内的 Deep Reading。Q-20260918-01 完整深读 Social Laws 一手研究的形式模型、alpha-robustness、Social-law 比较、Worst-case MDP Verification、近似 Value Bound、Grid 实验与边界。论文说明，单个 Agent 各自执行最优 Policy 并不能证明联合行为安全；在明确声明的 Stochastic-game Model 内，可以先求解每个 Single-agent Projection，再为每个 Agent 构造并求解一个 Worst-case MDP，从而验证共享 Action Restriction 的鲁棒性。关键边界是 alpha 不能单独作为采用依据，还必须同时看 Restriction 后保留下来的 Guaranteed Utility：规则更严格可能提高 Robustness，却降低实际效用；而 Guarantee 依赖完整声明的 State/Action/Reward/Transition Model、所有 Agent 均停留在假定 Policy Class 内，以及 Assumption 1 所要求的每个 State 都选择最优 Action。论文形式定义假定 Positive Reward，而实验使用全负 Cost；正文说明全负 Cost 可定义类似形式，但没有用同等细节重新推导。因此边界 Runtime 结论是 Coordination-rule Identity、Model Identity、Robustness Evidence、Utility Evidence、Execution Admission、Business Authorization 与 Effect Verification 必须保持为不同事实。Q-20260918-02 完整深读 Ask the Tool, Don't Guess 一手研究。研究区分可表示 Remaining Work 的 Strong Signal 与只能表示 Near-completion 的 Weak Signal，通过不改变 Agent-visible Result Path 的 Side Channel 输出 Call-id、Work-done、Total、Phase、Timestamp 进度事件，并显示 Live Progress 在 KV-cache 决策点及环境变化下明显优于基于历史 Duration 的 Predictor。4xH100 Serving Replay 中，相对 LRU 报告的 Tool Call 后 p90 TTFT 降幅为 HBM-only 20.7%、HBM+DRAM 20.8%。论文明确把 Tenant-originated Progress 视为 Untrusted Input，用 Session Credit 限制它对调度的影响，并把 Tool 不暴露信息、Parser 缺口和 Instrumentation 改变 Tool Behavior 列为边界。边界 Runtime 结论是 Execution Identity、Progress Observation、Telemetry Confidence、Scheduling Authority、Business Completion 与 Effect Authorization/Verification 必须分离；Progress 可以支持继续等待或资源重分配，但不能单独证明完成，更不能单独授权 Retry。Reading 未执行 Research Analysis、文章写作、可视化、Production 或 Publication。精确两份 Note Head 20d93522eeff716c8fe14be728e14572c41a1964 已在本 Result 持久化前通过 Validate Research Center 3.0 Run 35302389225 的 Validate Runtime Center 步骤。

reading.workResult: Skill 03 completed source-bounded Deep Reading for both same-date Selected objects. Q-20260917-01 read the complete EchoPath primary study and its appendices. EchoPath separates semantic retrieval from replay admission: executable memories require active lifecycle state, positive artifact validation, application/action compatibility, current state preconditions, bounded mutable parameters and current-screen target binding; ambiguous targets, failed state gates or non-flexible mutations reject direct replay and trigger bounded repair/planning fallback. In 159 active memories, Codex EchoPath completed 145/159 matched second-pass tasks (91.2%) at median 20,370 tokens and 127.5 seconds, while the reported Synapse planning baseline reached 91.8% at 586,386 median tokens and 315.7 seconds. State/flexible-input diagnostics further show that replay eligibility is a fresh observable decision, not a permanent property inherited from historical success. The bounded Runtime finding is that Memory Identity, Validation Identity, Current Compatibility, Replay Admission, Business Authorization and Effect Verification must remain separate facts; the GUI study does not establish authorization, idempotency or exactly-once external effects. Q-20260917-02 read the complete Emergence World Study 2 primary paper and appendices. Eight ten-agent worlds received phishing, misinformation and private-memory-breach stress events only after persistent operational state had accumulated. All seven exposed worlds warned peers about phishing, yet no world achieved complete defense across all three events; the best phishing score was 6/9, the best misinformation score 3/6, and only one world passed all five memory-breach criteria. Gemini recognized the phishing attack and warned peers but all ten agents still interacted with the attacker interface, producing 151 execution operations among 602 interactions; another agent attempted to retrieve an attack link about 46 hours after the active campaign had ended. The bounded architecture finding is Detection != Containment != Eradication != Recovery: persistent multi-agent Runtime needs threat identity, propagation/derivation evidence, quarantine authority, durable-state reconciliation and post-recovery verification rather than treating recognition or warning as a control. Reading performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production, Academic or Publication. The exact two-note head 9f44aa458de9ef1d7c2cf436acf9e602d7ec4ad7 passed Validate Research Center 3.0 run 35177726956 with conclusion success before this result was persisted.

triage.candidate: Interrupted long-running work may resume only by preserving and revalidating the prior authority, environment and work identity
triage.researchQuestion: After a managed runtime process restarts, which prior authority, environment and work-identity facts must remain true before an interrupted agent turn may continue without being treated as a new user request?

researchValue.failure: Persisted conversation state can survive a process restart while the interrupted operation's authority, environment or supersession status has changed, so blind continuation can duplicate work or act under stale authority.
researchValue.finding: The merged Codex implementation permits at most one continuation only when the restored thread is idle, permission profile matches, the same single local environment identity remains and an atomic previous-turn check shows no newer work superseded it.
researchValue.mechanism: Durably mark the old turn interrupted, carry recovery context internally rather than inventing a user message, then bind continuation to prior permission, local-environment identity and atomic supersession checks.
researchValue.implication: Autonomous recovery should be continuation of an already-authorized work identity, not authority inferred merely from durable conversation persistence.

triage.selectionReason: The authority-preserving continuation mechanism is concrete and adds interrupted-turn identity and supersession semantics beyond recent restart/recovery objects, but today's evidence remains one maintainer implementation. It is retained for cross-sample comparison rather than promoted over the stronger primary long-horizon study.

triage.candidate: Streaming transports need a stable logical-action identity boundary before tool calls reach side effects
triage.researchQuestion: When progressive streaming can expose repeated fragments for one logical function call, what deterministic identity should aggregation use so transport multiplicity cannot become duplicate external execution?

researchValue.failure: Progressive streaming can duplicate or lose logical function calls during aggregation, turning representation multiplicity into duplicate or missing external effects.
researchValue.finding: The merged ADK repair deduplicates stable model-issued function-call IDs and falls back to a canonical function-name plus sorted-arguments signature when a stable ID is unavailable.
researchValue.mechanism: Introduce a deterministic logical-call identity at aggregation before downstream tool execution, with regression tests for repeated calls both with and without model IDs.
researchValue.implication: Tool-call idempotency needs a boundary between transport fragments and logical actions; counting stream events is not sufficient identity.

triage.selectionReason: This is a concrete duplicate-effect prevention mechanism, but it remains one maintainer implementation. The Router Within supplies stronger primary comparative evidence and a distinct scalable-runtime question for today's Open-source Engineering slot.

triage.candidate: Long-horizon digital-employee success must separate semantic correctness from complete and timely operational execution
triage.researchQuestion: What evidence should prove that a long-running digital employee completed all required actions correctly and on time when semantic answer quality can remain high despite operational omissions and delay?

researchValue.failure: Correct diagnosis or short-task success can coexist with missed, incomplete or late critical actions across a full work shift.
researchValue.finding: Asclepius reports instruction-adherence drift, treatment incompleteness and severity-sensitive delay in full-shift traces, while its coupled adaptive harness improves held-out critical-action correctness by 22% and preserves diagnostic accuracy.
researchValue.mechanism: Evaluate full work episodes with separate semantic and action-completion metrics, then combine trace-driven manual revision, externalized skills and isolated subagent queue partitioning as the studied harness.
researchValue.implication: Digital-employee completion evidence must cover sustained operational obligations under time, resource and fairness constraints, not only local answer correctness.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary long-horizon evidence establishes a distinct completion-truth problem: correct understanding does not prove complete and timely work. It is sufficiently different from recent trace-attribution and checkpoint-consistency objects and has the highest Digital Employee research value today.

triage.candidate: Skill routing should be isolated as a measurable runtime component instead of scaling by permanent metadata preload
triage.researchQuestion: As an agent's skill catalog grows, can routing be separated from permanent context preload and evaluated independently for recall, context cost, latency and mid-rollout skill discovery?

researchValue.failure: Preloading an entire growing skill library consumes context and disperses attention, while external routing can separate selection logic from the agent model's own state.
researchValue.finding: The Router Within reports that frozen-model mid-layer states provide useful routing evidence across three public benchmarks plus 372 SkillTraj trajectories, with gains up to 13.4 points on written tasks and 21.9 points when skill need emerges mid-rollout in reported Qwen3-32B settings.
researchValue.mechanism: Construct compact skill banks, compare task and skill mid-layer states through two learned maps, shortlist skills and then combine shortlist evidence with the model's resumed forward-pass verdict.
researchValue.implication: Skill routing can become a separately testable runtime boundary with explicit quality and cost metrics rather than an implicit prompt convention.

triage.selectionReason: Primary benchmark evidence supports a bounded scalable-runtime question and provides stronger comparative evidence than today's single-implementation streaming-dedup signal. It also keeps the daily portfolio semantically diverse.

triage.candidate: Agent safety and admission evidence must bind to the exact post-transformation deployed artifact
triage.researchQuestion: When quantization or another deployment transformation can change agent behavior, which exact artifact identity, transformation provenance and revalidation evidence must be proven before the deployed agent may act?

researchValue.failure: An upstream full-precision checkpoint can appear benign during audit while the transformed deployment artifact later emits malicious structured function actions.
researchValue.finding: AGENTQ reports quantization-conditioned structured-action backdoors across NF4, FP4 and INT8, with attack success up to 100% after quantization in tested trigger-action pairs while retaining low benign-utility loss.
researchValue.mechanism: Construct behavior inside quantization-equivalence classes using layer-banded LoRA injection and partial-PGD repair so the post-quantization representation crosses into the attack behavior while the upstream checkpoint remains audit-benign.
researchValue.implication: Admission, provenance and safety evidence must identify and verify the artifact that will actually execute after deployment transformation rather than inherit trust from an upstream checkpoint by identity assumption.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary failure evidence establishes a high-value provenance and admission boundary around deployment transformation. The question is distinct from recent execution-lane admission because it concerns whether the tested artifact and the executing artifact remain behaviorally identical after transformation.

reading.workResult: Completed source-complete Deep Reading for all three same-date Selected objects without performing Research Analysis. Q-20260916-01 read Asclepius across the long-horizon CES simulator, baseline agents, self-evolving operating manual, external skills, isolated subagents, held-out protocol, ablations, failure-mode counters and limitations. The bounded finding is that semantic/diagnostic correctness and sustained operational completion are different evidence dimensions: the strong baseline scores 4.39/5 on diagnosis but 2.94/5 on critical actions, while full Asclepius reports a 22% held-out critical-action gain (p=0.024) with diagnosis preserved. The study is simulation-based, uses LLM graders and one rollout per configuration/batch, and does not establish clinical safety, authorization or exactly-once effects. Q-20260916-02 read AgentQ across the validation-deployment threat model, layer-banded low-rank injection, multi-codebook quantization-equivalence repair, six model scales across Qwen3.5/Hammer2.1, three trigger-action surfaces, NF4/FP4/INT8 results, utility/structured-output ablations, deployment case study, detection surface and limits. The bounded finding is that behavioral evidence attached only to an upstream full-precision checkpoint need not describe the transformed executable artifact: every constructed main-table checkpoint has measured FP16 ASR=0 on the tested attacks while every model/task cell exceeds 0.76 worst-codebook quantized ASR and 12/18 exceed 0.90. The source does not show that ordinary quantization is malicious or that all quantizers are equally vulnerable. Q-20260916-03 read The Router Within/Gavel across hidden-state glance, epsilon-cover skill banks, native verdict, product-of-experts ruling, training/calibration, three public benchmarks, 372 SkillTraj trajectories, live mini-swe-agent integration, ablations, adjudication and cost. The bounded finding is that skill routing can be isolated as a measurable Runtime component rather than permanent metadata preload; the reported Qwen3-32B setup reaches 90.9% correct-skill triggering on Skill-Use and leads the four SkillTraj scenarios, but correct routing is neither downstream task completion nor execution authorization. Reading created exactly three same-date Reading Notes and performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production, Academic or Publication.
reading.workResult_zh: 已对三个同日 Selected Object 完成来源完整 Deep Reading，未执行 Research Analysis。Q-20260916-01 完整深读 Asclepius 的长周期 CES 模拟器、Baseline Agent、自演化 Operating Manual、外部 Skills、隔离 Subagent、Held-out 协议、消融、失败计数与限制。有界结论是：Semantic/Diagnostic Correctness 与 Sustained Operational Completion 是不同证据维度；强 Baseline 的 Diagnosis 为 4.39/5，但 Critical Actions 仅 2.94/5，而 Full Asclepius 在保持 Diagnosis 的同时报告 Held-out Critical-action 提升 22%（p=0.024）。研究仍是模拟实验，依赖 LLM Grader，且每个 Configuration/Batch 只有一次 Rollout，不能证明临床安全、Authorization 或 Exactly-once Effect。Q-20260916-02 完整深读 AgentQ 的 Validation-deployment Threat Model、Layer-banded Low-rank Injection、Multi-codebook Quantization-equivalence Repair、Qwen3.5/Hammer2.1 两家族六个规模、三类 Trigger-action Surface、NF4/FP4/INT8 结果、Utility/Structured-output 消融、部署 Case Study、Detection Surface 与限制。有界结论是：只绑定 Full-precision 上游 Checkpoint 的行为证据不一定描述变换后的可执行 Artifact；主表中每个构造 Checkpoint 在所测攻击上的 FP16 ASR 均为 0，而全部 Model/Task Cell 的 Worst-codebook Quantized ASR 都高于 0.76，18 个中有 12 个高于 0.90。该来源不能推出普通量化本身具有恶意，也不能推出所有 Quantizer 同样脆弱。Q-20260916-03 完整深读 The Router Within/Gavel 的 Hidden-state Glance、Epsilon-cover Skill Bank、Native Verdict、Product-of-experts Ruling、Training/Calibration、三个公开 Benchmark、372 条 SkillTraj、mini-swe-agent 实际接入、消融、Adjudication 与 Cost。有界结论是：Skill Routing 可以作为独立可测 Runtime Component，而不是永久 Metadata Preload；所报告 Qwen3-32B 设置在 Skill-Use 上达到 90.9% Correct-skill Trigger，并在四种 SkillTraj Scenario 中领先，但正确 Routing 既不等于下游 Task Completion，也不等于 Execution Authorization。Reading 共形成 3 份同日 Reading Note，未执行 Research Analysis、文章写作、可视化、Production、Academic 或 Publication。

analysis.workResult: Applied Skill 04 to exactly three same-date source-complete Reading Notes and produced three bounded Research Objects. Q-20260916-01 concludes that consequential digital-employee completion should be represented as an evidence vector rather than a single success bit: semantic correctness, required-action closure, timeliness, priority/fairness obligations and episode/effect closure can fail independently, and every mandatory dimension must be proven or remain explicitly unresolved before business completion is accepted. triage.candidate: Managed agent harness and execution environment should remain separable trust boundaries
triage.researchQuestion: When a platform manages a long-running agent harness but allows multiple execution environments, which lifecycle responsibilities belong to the harness and which trust/authority facts must remain environment-owned?

researchValue.failure: Coupling harness lifecycle, context management and orchestration to one sandbox makes portability and trust boundaries opaque.
researchValue.finding: OpenAI exposes durable sessions, compaction, tool orchestration and subagents while keeping the sandbox selectable.
researchValue.mechanism: Managed harness services operate above a pluggable execution-environment boundary.
researchValue.implication: Agent platforms may need explicit contracts separating harness ownership from environment ownership and enforcement.

triage.selectionReason: The bounded architecture question is strong, but today's evidence is a single vendor public-beta announcement with no independent implementation, benchmark or incident. It therefore remains below Skill 02's preferred evidence-sufficiency threshold.

triage.candidate: Recovery across service restart must re-prove operation-specific authority and readiness facts
triage.researchQuestion: After a provisioning service restarts mid-operation, which identity, ownership and readiness facts must be re-established before registration may resume and before execution may proceed?

researchValue.failure: Transport reconnection after restart can be mistaken for proof that partially progressed side effects remain safe to continue.
researchValue.finding: The merged implementation bounds restart retry, authenticates the replacement service and separates registration-resume eligibility from runtime readiness.
researchValue.mechanism: Revalidate identity and ownership/state invariants for the operation while keeping runtime readiness as a stricter downstream gate.
researchValue.implication: Recovery should restore only the authority facts needed for the specific operation, not infer full execution readiness from connectivity.

triage.selectionReason: The mechanism is concrete and governance-relevant, but it remains one maintainer implementation. LAST-CQ supplies stronger primary comparative evidence for today's single Open-source Engineering slot.

triage.candidate: Agent handoff must preserve the caller's waiting and checkpoint truth
triage.researchQuestion: When control transfers across agent parent contexts and the target pauses for human input, which execution context owns the Waiting state, interrupt evidence and resumable checkpoint?

researchValue.failure: A transferred agent can be waiting for human input while the caller is falsely recorded Completed and no checkpoint is produced.
researchValue.finding: The bug came from interrupt evidence being attached to the wrong parent context; the merged fix returns interrupt IDs to the caller and propagates resume inputs through scheduling.
researchValue.mechanism: Bind interrupt and checkpoint evidence to the context whose runner owns completion semantics across the handoff.
researchValue.implication: Delegation changes execution location but must not sever the responsibility context that determines Waiting, completion and resumability.

triage.selectionReason: This is a strong completion-truth failure with a clear handoff mechanism, but evidence is still one maintainer implementation. It is retained for future cross-sample comparison rather than promoted on implementation evidence alone.

triage.candidate: Recovery loops should justify each component by causal contribution, not by architectural intuition
triage.researchQuestion: Which components of a bounded agent recovery loop actually cause recovery gains once failure detection, retry, feedback sophistication and parallel sampling are separated counterfactually?

researchValue.failure: Complex reflection or extra sampling can consume cost without causing the recovery gain attributed to the overall loop.
researchValue.finding: Across 2,471 live-database queries, six backbones and counterfactual variants, correction/retry drives most of the gain, feedback sophistication changes little and equal-budget parallel sampling degrades quality; 91.7% of single-pass failures are recovered.
researchValue.mechanism: Use execution-grounded failure detection to route a bounded correction attempt and measure loop components counterfactually.
researchValue.implication: Recovery architecture should earn complexity with causal evidence rather than assuming more feedback or more samples are better.

triage.selectionReason: Strong primary counterfactual evidence directly answers a bounded engineering question about causal recovery value and is distinct from permission, replay-safety and checkpoint-consistency research.

triage.candidate: Reflection should be scheduled against a finite retry budget rather than treated as an always-on improvement
triage.researchQuestion: Under a fixed attempt budget, when should a long-running agent exploit reflected lessons and when should it preserve budget for continued exploration?

researchValue.failure: Always-on reflection can consume finite retries and suppress exploration, reducing success in some environments.
researchValue.finding: VRL-Bench reports sign-changing effects for reflection/memory updates and a robust positive gain only for the tested VEX2 policy across all six settings.
researchValue.mechanism: Evaluate learning policy under a fixed trial budget and schedule remaining attempts between exploitation of remembered lessons and exploration.
researchValue.implication: Retry budgets should be explicit and reflection should be conditional rather than assumed beneficial.

triage.selectionReason: The evidence is strong enough for selection, but choosing it alongside LAST-CQ would concentrate today's portfolio on closely related retry/reflection mechanics. It remains a high-priority candidate for a later recovery-budget study.

triage.candidate: Persistent-agent memory needs explicit temporal commitment semantics for durable and transient state
triage.researchQuestion: What lifecycle semantics should distinguish transient observations from durable knowledge so temporary context cannot silently become long-term agent state?

researchValue.failure: Shared write semantics let transient observations overwrite stable memory and cause behavioral drift.
researchValue.finding: Lifecycle labels, separate stable/transient components and phase-aware readout reduce temporary overwrite in the authors' controlled benchmark while remaining broadly competitive on two public long-memory benchmarks.
researchValue.mechanism: Tag writes by temporal commitment, maintain stable and transient stores separately and make readout lifecycle-aware.
researchValue.implication: Persistent digital employees may need memory governance that specifies not just what may be stored but how long a fact may influence future work.

triage.selectionReason: The primary research supports a distinct memory-governance question about write/read lifecycle commitment, with enough distance from recent migration and evidence-preservation objects to provide new research value while keeping today's portfolio diverse.

reading.workResult: Completed source-complete Deep Reading for both same-date Selected objects without performing Research Analysis. Q-20260915-01 read LifeFuse-Mem across lifecycle definitions, stable/plastic update routing, controlled anti-overwrite protocol, public long-memory compatibility checks, ablations and limits. The controlled 1,000-episode experiment supports a bounded finding that explicit lifecycle-labelled writes, supervised routing and phase-aware protected readout can reduce temporary overwrite of acquired permanent facts, while the strongest reported configurations still retain substantial overwrite. The paper assumes lifecycle labels and phase/query lifecycle are already known; it does not demonstrate autonomous lifecycle discovery, transient-to-durable promotion, revocation after contradiction, production latency/storage behavior, or authority to classify a memory as durable. Q-20260915-02 read LAST-CQ across its five-stage architecture, 2,471 live-database queries, six backbones, independent and counterfactual baselines, recovery calculations, feedback ablation, equal-budget parallel sampling, judge calibration, failure categories and limitations. The bounded finding is that execution-grounded failure detection plus explicit recovery routing and one bounded retry recover a large share of initial failures in this structured domain (91.7% unweighted mean recovery; 93.8% pooled), while richer grounded feedback adds only about one point in aggregate exact-match and equal-budget Best-of-3 can perform worse. The study does not establish semantic correctness from non-empty execution, general retry safety for state-changing tools, authorization continuity, exactly-once effects, or cross-domain transfer. Reading created exactly two same-date Reading Notes and performed no Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production or Publication.

triage.candidate: Environment-scoped identity policy should constrain per-agent authentication choices
triage.researchQuestion: Which identity modes may an enterprise agent choose locally, and which must be constrained by environment-level governance before the agent is admitted?

researchValue.failure: Per-agent authentication choice can fragment enterprise identity policy and leave unsupported or anonymous access paths active.
researchValue.finding: Microsoft exposes tenant/environment controls that constrain allowed authentication modes outside individual agent configuration.
researchValue.mechanism: Bind agent authentication options to environment-scoped policy and enforce the allowed identity modes centrally.
researchValue.implication: Enterprise agent identity is a control-plane contract rather than a purely local agent setting.

triage.selectionReason: The mechanism is governance-relevant and bounded, but today it is supported by one vendor's official documentation and substantially touches recent authority-policy research. It needs an independent implementation, failure result or comparative sample before selection.

triage.candidate: Workspace, session, authorization context and cleanup ownership need one lifecycle lineage
triage.researchQuestion: How should a long-running agent bind workspace identity, session identity, inherited approval context and cleanup ownership so partial startup failure does not orphan or destroy useful state?

researchValue.failure: Separate informal workspace/session steps can orphan checkouts, lose approval context or delete useful state during partial failure.
researchValue.finding: Codex coordinates worktree creation, session binding, inherited reviewer context and cleanup ownership in one merged lifecycle path.
researchValue.mechanism: Resolve a source branch, create and bind the session before user work, pause conflicting actions and clean only unclaimed clean worktrees.
researchValue.implication: Durable lineage is needed across workspace identity, session identity, authorization context and cleanup ownership.

triage.selectionReason: The lifecycle binding is concrete and high-value, but it remains one Codex maintainer implementation and partially neighbors recent recovery/workspace-lineage research. Independent comparison is needed before promotion.

triage.candidate: Configured policy provenance must remain separate from effective sandbox capability
triage.researchQuestion: When runtime capability is selected by explicit configuration or fallback, which provenance must be preserved so later host-admission and audit decisions can distinguish operator intent from effective enforcement?

researchValue.failure: Flattening effective sandbox state loses whether enforcement came from explicit policy or fallback and makes later audit ambiguous.
researchValue.finding: The implementation preserves configured mode separately from effective sandbox level.
researchValue.mechanism: Prepare and validate effective sandbox configuration while retaining whether the operator explicitly configured the mode.
researchValue.implication: Host admission should record declared policy, fallback source and effective capability as separate facts.

triage.selectionReason: The configured-versus-effective distinction is a strong audit mechanism, but today it is supported by one maintainer implementation and does not outrank the primary-research evaluation object in this column.

triage.candidate: Execution-lane-specific admission facts should replace one universal host probe
triage.researchQuestion: Which credential, provider and host facts must be proven for the selected execution lane, and which dependencies must not gate a worker when they are irrelevant to that lane?

researchValue.failure: A provider-valid API key on a clean machine was rejected because direct API execution inherited an irrelevant local subscription-CLI probe.
researchValue.finding: The release smoke demonstrated that direct API-key and local subscription execution require different admission evidence.
researchValue.mechanism: Re-verify API-key credentials at the provider boundary while retaining the local CLI hello probe only for subscription execution.
researchValue.implication: Admission contracts should bind requirements to the chosen execution lane instead of applying universal host dependencies.

triage.selectionReason: A clean-machine release-gate failure plus the merged correction supplies a strong bounded primary failure result. It establishes a distinct admission-contract question rather than another generic authority-precedence object.

triage.candidate: MCP transport lifetime, security and resumability should be operator-owned protocol state
triage.researchQuestion: Which HTTP transport limits, security controls and replay/resumability assumptions must a product own explicitly instead of inheriting from dependency defaults?

researchValue.failure: Transitive dependency defaults can silently change session, security or replay semantics between otherwise similar deployments.
researchValue.finding: The draft identifies missing operator ownership over timeout, session caps, body limits, DNS-rebinding protection and event-store resumability.
researchValue.mechanism: Expose transport behavior in product-owned configuration, validate incompatible combinations and optionally bind bearer tokens to the MCP resource.
researchValue.implication: Protocol compatibility should include a versioned runtime transport contract, not merely endpoint reachability.

triage.selectionReason: The problem is legitimate and bounded, but the current evidence is an open draft/unverified discussion rather than merged or independently validated behavior.

triage.candidate: Trace-level evaluation should attribute trust failures to lifecycle stages instead of final task status
triage.researchQuestion: What structured execution evidence is required to identify where an agent failed when final task completion can coexist with unsafe tool use, ungrounded reasoning or execution-integrity violations?

researchValue.failure: Task-level pass/fail can hide unsafe compliance, ungrounded reasoning or execution-integrity failures.
researchValue.finding: Models with similar completion behavior can diverge materially in unsafe-compliance classifications when evaluated from full traces.
researchValue.mechanism: Evaluate recorded traces across lifecycle dimensions and attribute failures to the responsible stage.
researchValue.implication: Independent EVAL needs structured runtime evidence sufficient to locate failure, not merely a final deliverable.

triage.selectionReason: Primary benchmark evidence supplies a direct evaluation finding with a bounded trace-attribution question. It is distinct from prior evaluator-independence and audit-coverage research because it isolates failure-attribution granularity inside an observed trace.

triage.candidate: Multi-agent coordination reliability should be decomposed into allocation, ordering, exclusion and handoff
triage.researchQuestion: Which coordination constructs must be tested separately before aggregate task success can support a claim that an agent team is reliable?

researchValue.failure: Aggregate success can conceal that a team is reliable at allocation but weak at mutual exclusion or handoff.
researchValue.finding: Across 897 oracle-validated tasks and 11 multimodal models, coordination competence is construct-specific rather than one scalar capability.
researchValue.mechanism: Evaluate executable tasks with construct-level diagnostics for allocation, ordering, mutual exclusion and handoff alongside overall completion.
researchValue.implication: Multi-agent systems should validate coordination contracts separately before inferring overall team reliability.

triage.selectionReason: The primary benchmark provides strong cross-model evidence for a distinct construct-level coordination question and is materially different from recent work on deterministic manager functions.

triage.candidate: Human-facing progress communication should remain a manager-scoped capability rather than a generic subagent tool
triage.researchQuestion: Which agent role should have authority to communicate asynchronous progress to a human when internal subagents are still working, and how should that capability preserve responsibility topology?
triage.selectionReason: The root-versus-subagent communication boundary is concrete and governance-relevant, but today it is supported by one Codex maintainer implementation. It needs an independent implementation, failure study or comparative sample before selection.

triage.candidate: Cancellation may preserve cleanup obligations without becoming business completion
triage.researchQuestion: Which lifecycle cleanup obligations must still run after cancellation, and how can a runtime execute them exactly once without replacing the original cancellation with a false completion signal?
triage.selectionReason: The cancellation/finalization separation is a bounded engineering mechanism with targeted tests, but it remains one maintainer implementation and lacks independent comparative or incident evidence.

triage.candidate: Concurrent agent state requires a type-aware merge contract beyond last-writer-wins
triage.researchQuestion: When parallel workers update shared state, which merge semantics prevent silent loss without converting duplicate or conflicting effects into apparently valid state?
triage.selectionReason: The list-concatenation change clearly exposes the failure of generic last-writer-wins and preserves an explicit duplicate caveat, but one implementation is not enough to establish the broader concurrency contract as today's selected object.

triage.candidate: Audit-process completion must be separated from evidence-coverage completion
triage.researchQuestion: What evidence must demonstrate coverage before an AI-assisted audit may claim completion when an agentic search can finish yet miss relevant cases?
triage.selectionReason: A disclosed missed-case failure directly falsifies the inference that a completed agentic search proves audit coverage. Although the source was also used on September 10, today's bounded question concerns audit evidence coverage rather than high-impact execution authority and live enforcement, so it is not a duplicate research problem.

triage.candidate: Long-horizon recovery needs aligned checkpoints of cognitive and environment state
triage.researchQuestion: Which cognitive and environment/effect state must share a checkpoint identity so a long-running agent can recover from propagated errors without resuming against an inconsistent world?
triage.selectionReason: The paper supplies a primary mechanism plus measured comparison across tasks, models, execution strategies and harnesses, and asks a distinct recovery-state question not covered by recent memory-evidence or interrupted-call replay objects.
